jobs.title: Senior Vice President IT - Generation, Transmission & Distribution
jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date

10-19-2026

Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

We are seeking a forward-thinking and transformational Senior Vice President, Information Technology - Generation, Transmission & Distribution who will report directly to the Executive Vice President and Chief Information & Technology Officer. This executive will define and execute the technology vision and strategy that powers the company's generation, transmission, and distribution operations while enabling innovation, resilience, and business growth across the enterprise. The role provides executive leadership for technology platforms, digital capabilities, and operational systems supporting the company's critical infrastructure and field operations. The SVP will also lead technology readiness, integration, and optimization efforts related to mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and large-scale transformation initiatives.

Accountable for technology strategy, portfolio management, service delivery, and business outcomes, the SVP will champion modernization, digital transformation, operational excellence, reliability, cybersecurity, and workforce enablement across Generation, Transmission, and Distribution. This leader will cultivate strong partnerships with business executives and stakeholders to ensure technology investments deliver measurable value, support strategic priorities, and advance the company's commitment to safe, reliable, and efficient operations.

Job Description

What You'll Do:

Strategic Leadership & Vision

Develop and execute a comprehensive technology strategy supporting Generation, Transmission, Distribution, and related business functions.
Establish an enterprise-wide digital roadmap that advances operational excellence, business performance, grid modernization, generation optimization, and long-term enterprise objectives.
Align technology investments with strategic priorities, regulatory requirements, cybersecurity standards, and measurable business outcomes.
Lead modernization initiatives that enhance safety, reliability, resiliency, asset performance, operational efficiency, and workforce productivity.
Identify and assess emerging technologies that create competitive advantages and support the evolution of a more intelligent, connected, and sustainable utility.

Technology Leadership & Expertise

Provide executive oversight of technology platforms supporting:

Generation Operations and Asset Performance
Transmission and Distribution Operations
GIS and Network Modeling
Engineering and Design Systems
Construction and Capital Project Management
Grid Planning and Analytics
Field Mobility and Workforce Solutions
Outage Planning and Management Integration
Generation SCADA and Market Operations
Fuels Management and Settlements
Environmental and Compliance Management
Vegetation and Infrastructure Management
Production Accounting and Performance Management
Telecommunications and Field Communications Technologies

Additional responsibilities include:

Drive modernization through Artificial Intelligence (AI), cloud technologies, scalable architectures, enterprise integration platforms, and modern application ecosystems.
Champion Agile delivery, DevSecOps, API-first architecture, automation, and modern software engineering practices that improve speed, quality, security, reliability, and reuse across the technology organization.
Lead enterprise adoption of AI, machine learning, digital twins, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and optimization technologies to improve safety, reliability, affordability, and customer outcomes.
Ensure technology platforms operate as an integrated ecosystem supporting seamless data and process flow across the asset lifecycle.

Business Partnership

Serve as the primary technology partner for Generation, Transmission, and Distribution leadership.
Translate business priorities and operational challenges into measurable technology outcomes.
Support end-to-end utility asset lifecycle management from planning and design through construction, operations, maintenance, optimization, and retirement.\
Lead technology investment planning, portfolio prioritization, business case development, and value realization efforts.
Establish and maintain strategic vendor and partner relationships that advance business and technology objectives.
Serve as the accountable Service Owner for technology platforms supporting Generation, Transmission, and Distribution, with responsibility for performance, risk, and business outcomes.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

Ensure compliance with cybersecurity standards, regulatory mandates, environmental requirements, reliability standards, and enterprise governance policies.
Establish governance processes and decision frameworks for technology portfolios, investments, architecture, and delivery performance.
Own technology financial performance, budget management, investment prioritization, and return-on-investment accountability.
Advance enterprise data governance, data quality, and information management capabilities.
Partner closely with cybersecurity and operational technology leaders to maintain secure, resilient, and compliant technology environments.

Talent & Culture Development

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing technology organization supporting utility operational excellence.
Create leadership pipelines, succession plans, and talent development programs that strengthen organizational capability.
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer focus.
Develop leaders capable of thinking beyond functional silos to drive enterprise-wide impact.
Promote inclusion, learning, and engagement while attracting and retaining top technology talent.

Thought Leadership & Enterprise Impact

Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on technology trends, digital transformation opportunities, and business innovation.
Represent the company in industry forums, regulatory discussions, technology councils, and strategic partnerships.
Lead enterprise conversations around AI, operational intelligence, advanced analytics, and emerging utility technologies.
Drive technology strategies that improve reliability, resilience, affordability, safety, sustainability, and customer satisfaction.
Support enterprise transformation initiatives, including mergers, acquisitions, integrations, and major organizational change programs.

What We're Looking For:

Education:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related discipline required.
Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Information Technology, or related field preferred.

Experience:

15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience within utility operations, energy, engineering, infrastructure, manufacturing, or other asset-intensive industries.

Other Must Haves:

Demonstrated success leading large-scale technology organizations and enterprise digital transformation initiatives.
Deep expertise in operational technologies, asset management, utility operations, engineering systems, enterprise applications, data analytics, and technology modernization.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect technology strategy to operational and financial outcomes.
Proven ability to lead complex portfolios, large budgets, strategic investments, and executive stakeholder relationships.
Exceptional communication, organizational leadership, and change management skills.
Deep knowledge of electric utility operations, including Generation, Transmission, Distribution, and asset lifecycle management.
Experience with grid modernization, renewable energy technologies, market operations, and emerging energy technologies.
Expertise in enterprise asset management, GIS, engineering systems, predictive maintenance, digital twins, advanced analytics, and AI-enabled solutions.
Proven track record driving enterprise-wide organizational transformation and technology adoption.
Experience leading technology integration activities associated with mergers, acquisitions, and business transformation efforts.

Where You'll Work:

On-Site in the AEP Headquarters in Columbus, OH

What You'll Get:

Base salary
Annual bonus
Long-term incentive
401K match
AEP Pension
Comprehensive benefits package that aims to support and enhance the overall well-being of our employees.

Where Putting the Customer First Powers Everything We Do!

At AEP, we’re more than just an energy company — we’re a team of dedicated professionals committed to delivering safe, reliable, and innovative energy solutions. Guided by our mission to put the customer first, we strive to exceed expectations by listening, responding, and continuously improving the way we serve our communities. If you're passionate about making a meaningful impact and being part of a forward-thinking organization, this is the company for you!

jobs.title: VP, Information Technology
jobs.description:
Viventium Software Inc. is a SaaS-based human capital management solution that provides a remarkable user experience and award- winning software. Viventium provides flexible software and expert guidance so clients can be sure their payroll is done right.

Viventium offers specialized solutions in the health services markets which include home care agencies and skilled nursing facilities. Viventium Software supports all fifty of the United States with payroll and HR solutions.

Relax - you’re with Viventium.

Position Summary

The Vice President, Information Technology (VP, IT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the strategy, security, and day-to-day execution of Viventium’s global corporate IT and information security functions. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the VP, IT leads the design, delivery, and operation of technology and security solutions that support the organization’s goals across its U.S., Costa Rica, United Kingdom, Canada, and India operations, and is responsible for ensuring the security, integrity, and availability of the company’s data and IT infrastructure.

This role combines strategic planning with hands-on operational delivery. The VP, IT owns enterprise IT service delivery, cybersecurity operations, regulatory and audit compliance (e.g., SOC 1 / SOC 2), vendor and license management, and the technology integration of acquired businesses.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The essential functions include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develops and executes long- and short-term strategic and operational plans for corporate IT and security that align with company priorities, business needs, service and operational excellence, resource planning, and growth at scale.
Manages and oversees the comprehensive enterprise information security (InfoSec) program to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the company’s platforms, data, applications, networks, systems, servers, and endpoints in an operationally efficient and effective manner.
Leads security operations, monitoring, and incident response in partnership with the company’s managed SOC/EDR provider; performs risk analysis for existing and potential partners and providers.
Owns regulatory and audit compliance, including SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 evidence, the risk register, internal controls matrix, and coordination with external auditors and cyber-insurance carriers.
Directs enterprise IT service delivery, endpoint management, identity and access management, and end-user enablement across a distributed, multi-country workforce.
Leads the technology and security integration of acquired businesses, including identity, email, SSO, security-baseline alignment, backup/DR readiness, and vendor consolidation.
Establishes and enforces a Microsoft-first enterprise tooling strategy and AI governance framework (e.g., Microsoft 365, Purview, Copilot, Azure AI Foundry) with clear governance guardrails for approved AI tools.
Oversees management of third-party vendors in collaboration with Finance — including software, IT hardware, desktop services, telephony, managed services, data center, and network services — and enforces IT procurement and spend-governance policy.
Develops, submits, and manages the operational and capital budget requirements for technology solutions; submits regular progress reports on timeliness, performance, quality, and cost.
Oversees and governs Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery planning for all IT assets and systems.
Institutes and enforces security policy, frameworks, and procedures; balances information assurance with productivity; ensures regulatory compliance; and educates staff on the ethical and secure use of company resources.
Attracts, develops, mentors, and retains top technology and security talent; builds a resilient team structure that minimizes single points of failure.
Supports a culture of client service, continual improvement, and cross-functional collaboration within IT and throughout the company; serves as a role model of integrity and results-oriented focus.

Qualifications

Technology leadership background including experience serving as CIO, VP of IT, or Head of IT, with a proven track record of leading people and managing departmental operations and finances. Expertise implementing InfoSec policies and solutions is of critical importance.
Proven experience leading enterprise IT and security in a regulated, multi-entity, and/or multi-country environment; experience with SaaS, HCM, payroll, or healthcare-adjacent businesses preferred.
Demonstrated experience owning SOC 1 / SOC 2 (or comparable) audit and compliance programs.
Proven experience leading digital enterprise transformation and implementing modern technologies such as cloud, identity, data/analytics, and AI to enable productivity and growth at scale.
Experience leading post-acquisition technology integration (identity, email, SSO, security baseline, vendor consolidation).
Strong project management, vendor management, and budget-management skills.
Excellent business acumen combined with creative problem-solving and analytical skills; a strategic thinker able to see beyond what is and imagine what should be.
Strong negotiator and communicator, able to build credibility with senior business leaders and drive change through influence and persuasion.
High degree of entrepreneurial spirit and initiative; willing to “roll up sleeves” and operate hands-on.
Ability to attract, develop, mentor, and retain top technology talent; sophisticated approach to multi-stakeholder relationship management.
Occasional travel to Viventium facilities (including Costa Rica) and industry conferences.

jobs.description:

Beeline UAS is an FAA Part 135 air carrier operating drone delivery for enterprise and healthcare partners across the United States. We are a small, senior team opening new metropolitan operating areas, and our systems need to grow with us.

You are Beeline's IT lead on a fractional basis. You own our device fleet, identity and security posture, and the software stack our crews and regulators depend on. Manage the Microsoft 365 tenant, devices, and access controls for crewmembers at remote hubs and the ROCC.

Own security policy and practice: MFA, conditional access, endpoint protection, backup, and incident response appropriate to an air carrier handling partner and patient-adjacent data.

Lead platform decisions and migrations as the company scales.

Build and maintain integrations between flight operations tools and compliance workflows, and FAA-acceptable records and signatures.

Experience running IT for a small, distributed company, ideally in a regulated industry (aviation, healthcare, or similar).

Deep hands-on skill with Microsoft 365, Intune, Entra ID, and SharePoint.

Contract, remote (U.S.), $3,000 per month retainer, estimated 20 to 40 hours per month to start.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Healthcare IT
jobs.description:
CORMAC is seeking an experienced Program Manager to provide strategic leadership, operational oversight, and successful execution of complex federal healthcare technology initiatives. This role is responsible for managing program performance across cost, schedule, quality, risk, compliance, and customer satisfaction while leading multidisciplinary teams operating within modern Agile delivery environments.

The Program Manager will serve as the primary liaison between executive stakeholders, customer representatives, and delivery teams, ensuring successful execution of technology modernization, application development, operations and maintenance, cloud-based solutions, and data-driven initiatives. The ideal candidate is a proven leader with experience managing large-scale federal IT programs, directing cross-functional teams, and driving delivery excellence within highly regulated environments.

Key Responsibilities

Provide overall management and executive oversight of CMS, including contract performance, staffing, financials, risk management, and reporting to the stakeholders

Lead and coordinate multiple Agile sprint teams and Kanban teams (for example quality measures, reporting and dashboards, data operations, DevOps, and security) using the SAFe framework

Serve as the primary point of contact for CMS program office staff and ensure continuous, transparent collaboration, including on-site engagement in Baltimore, MD when needed

Plan and sequence work around the annual federal rulemaking cycle and mandates such as the ACA and the IMPACT Act, incorporating policy changes and shocks into operations and maintenance schedules

Oversee management of the CMSmeasure inventory and the impact assessment of new, modified, or removed quality measures across provider types

Govern integration dependencies across the provider demographic data sources, and the CMS AWS Cloud environment

Oversee Tier 3 production support through ServiceNow, including incident and problem management, root cause analysis, and coordinated deployments

Ensure deliverables and platform operations comply with FISMA, FedRAMP, ARS 5, ATO requirements, Zero Trust directives, HIPAA, NIST, and Section 508 accessibility requirements

Conduct Monthly Project Reviews and executive oversight briefings, and maintain project controls, quality management processes, and knowledge transfer practices aligned to CMMI Maturity Level 3 and ISO 9001

Evaluate and govern responsible adoption of AI-enabled tooling to improve software development efficiency and reduce manual review effort

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, Health Informatics, or a similar field

Must be a U.S. Citizen

Must be able to obtain a Public Trust (Tier I) Clearance

Minimum of 10+ years of progressive experience managing complex IT programs, including prior experience as a program or project manager on federal contracts

Demonstrated experience leading multiple Agile teams under SAFe, Scrum, or Kanban, including release planning and stakeholder feedback loops

Experience managing the full application lifecycle for cloud-hosted applications, including operations and maintenance and production support

Working knowledge of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) programs, with familiarity with quality reporting, Medicare data.

Experience managing to federal security and compliance requirements such as FISMA, FedRAMP, NIST, and HIPAA

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to brief Government leadership and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment

Preferred Qualifications:

Master's degree in a relevant field

Experience supporting CMS quality reporting programs such as Hospital, Hospice, Nursing Home, or Post-Acute Care Quality Reporting Programs

Experience with CMS AWS Cloud environments and CMS enterprise authentication frameworks (HARP/IDM). Hands on hands-on AWS skills will be a huge plus

Project Management Professional (PMP), SAFe Program Consultant (SPC), or equivalent certification

Experience managing programs operating under CMMI Maturity Level 3 and ISO 9001 quality processes

Experience managing CPARS-reviewed federal contracts and Firm-Fixed-Price or Time-and-Materials contract structures

Experience introducing AI/LLM-enabled tooling into delivery workflows in a federal setting

Why CORMAC?

At CORMAC, we leverage the power of Data Management and Analytics to enable our customers to achieve their strategic goals. With over 20 years of experience in Health Information Technology (HIT), human-centered design principles and Agile development methodologies, CORMAC delivers complex digital solutions to solve some of the most challenging problems facing public healthcare programs today.

As a US Federal Government contractor in the public healthcare sector, our work is impactful and cutting-edge while being performed in a supportive, collaborative, and welcoming environment. We offer flexible work schedules with remote, hybrid, or fully in-person workplace options to empower our employees to decide the workplace most suitable for them. At CORMAC, we have a highly diverse workforce, and believe the work environment is a place where creativity, collaboration, enthusiasm, and innovation happens, regardless of location.

jobs.title: 1717 - Senior Manager, Indirect Procurement- IT
jobs.description:
LogicSource
is an innovative leader in sourcing and procurement services, helping companies increase profits through better buying. Operated by a 500-person collective of procurement professionals, we are deeply rooted in data and insight-driven strategic sourcing, category management, operational excellence, and value delivery. Partnering with Fortune 500 companies, we build and nurture strategic relationships while delivering strong execution that drives measurable bottom-line impact and the development of best-in-class procurement capabilities. Learn more about us at www.logicsource.com.

Reasons Why You’ll Love It Here

A collaborative, supportive culture where your contributions are valued, and your work makes a meaningful impact.
A workplace committed to professional growth with paths to development and advancement.
Dedicated to creating an environment for employee success by providing support for long-term career growth.
Committed to work-life balance by offering flexible PTO.
A robust benefits package that includes extensive health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family. Employer‑funded HRA, a 401(k) match, Healthcare and Dependent Care FSAs, short- and long-term disability coverage, AD&D, life insurance, fertility assistance, and more.
Supplemental benefits such as unexpected large expenses related to Accidents, Hospitalization, or Critical Care. Along with support for Maternity/Paternity, FMLA, and Military leave.
Offer behavioral health services within the medical support insurance plan and everyday support tools to help with mental health.
A business-casual workplace offering a flexible, hybrid work environment with offices in Westport, CT, and Charleston, SC.

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Indirect Procurement- IT is a client-facing leader responsible for owning and leading category strategy on behalf of our client. Acting as the accountable category owner, this role defines the strategic direction, owns IT category planning, and orchestrates delivery through a centralized Center of Excellence (COE) to execute sourcing initiatives and contract negotiations. The Senior Manager, serves as a trusted advisor to clients, translating business objectives into actionable category strategies that deliver measurable value.

Responsibilities

Client Advisory & IT Category Leadership
Serve as the primary strategic category leader and execution partner for assigned client and category or categories.
Partner with client and functional leaders to understand business objectives, constraints, and priorities.
Translate client goals into clear category strategies, value levers, and execution-ready roadmaps.

Category Strategy & Planning
Own and support the development and ongoing management of category strategies, including market analysis, spend diagnostics, supplier landscape assessments, and risk considerations.
Lead and support annual and multi-year category planning, defining initiatives, savings targets, timelines, and success metrics.
Continuously refine category and vendor strategies based on market shifts, client needs, and performance results.

Center of Excellence (COE) Orchestration
Leverage a centralized COE to deliver sourcing events, negotiations, and contract execution on behalf of the client.
Set strategic direction and priorities for COE resources, ensuring alignment to client objectives.
Provide governance, decision support, and hands-on quality oversight throughout sourcing and contracting cycles.

Sourcing, Negotiation & Contract Execution
Create and execute effective go-to-market and negotiation strategies in line with commercial objectives and supplier positioning.
Directly support and lead components of complex, high-value, or highly sensitive negotiations.
Review and support sourcing recommendations, supplier selections, and contract structures to ensure value realization and risk mitigation.

Value Delivery & Performance Management
Own and manage category-level performance, including savings, value creation, service levels, and risk outcomes.
Proactively identify and execute incremental opportunities for value, optimization, efficiency, and innovation.

Stakeholder & Supplier Engagement
Build and maintain strong relationships with client stakeholders.
Facilitate alignment across client procurement, finance, legal, and business teams to enable timely decision-making and delivery.
Engage strategically with key suppliers to drive performance, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Leadership & Practice Contribution
Apply, execute, and continuously improve established methodologies, tools, and best practices across client engagements.
Contribute to the evolution of category management frameworks, playbooks, and intellectual capital by identifying operational efficiency opportunities and practical improvements.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
7+ years of experience in category management, strategic sourcing, contract lifecycle, and vendor management. Proven experience developing and executing category strategies and delivering measurable results Demonstrated success influencing stakeholders in complex, matrixed environments.
Experience managing vendor relationships and leading high-value contract negotiations.
Experience in complex spend analysis, total cost of ownership (TCO), and financial modeling to support category and sourcing decisions.
Highly skilled in diplomacy, consensus-building, and cross-functional leadership.
Entrepreneurial mindset with a strong commitment to client service and value creation.
Polished communicator and presenter, both formally and informally.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel-based financial analysis and PowerPoint presentations.
Strong problem-solving, judgment, and leadership capabilities.
Ability to operate strategically.

Measures Of Success

Delivery of committed client value (savings, cost avoidance, and broader business outcomes).
Deliver engagements on time and accurately, meeting scope, quality, and milestone commitments.
Execute category and sourcing initiatives using fact‑based analysis (e.g., spend, TCO, cost models).
Achieve strong sourcing and contract outcomes that enable value realization post‑award.
Maintain high stakeholder satisfaction through clear communication and execution credibility.

Travel:
This position will require some travel.

This Position Description is not an exhaustive list of the duties and responsibilities, and the employee is expected to perform other duties as necessary and assigned. The duties and responsibilities of this position may be modified at any time to meet changing business needs.

new_jobs.description:
Viventium Software Inc. is a SaaS-based human capital management solution that provides a remarkable user experience and award- winning software. Viventium provides flexible software and expert guidance so clients can be sure their payroll is done right.

Viventium offers specialized solutions in the health services markets which include home care agencies and skilled nursing facilities. Viventium Software supports all fifty of the United States with payroll and HR solutions.

Relax - you’re with Viventium.

Position Summary

The Vice President, Information Technology (VP, IT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the strategy, security, and day-to-day execution of Viventium’s global corporate IT and information security functions. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the VP, IT leads the design, delivery, and operation of technology and security solutions that support the organization’s goals across its U.S., Costa Rica, United Kingdom, Canada, and India operations, and is responsible for ensuring the security, integrity, and availability of the company’s data and IT infrastructure.

This role combines strategic planning with hands-on operational delivery. The VP, IT owns enterprise IT service delivery, cybersecurity operations, regulatory and audit compliance (e.g., SOC 1 / SOC 2), vendor and license management, and the technology integration of acquired businesses.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The essential functions include, but are not limited to, the following:

Develops and executes long- and short-term strategic and operational plans for corporate IT and security that align with company priorities, business needs, service and operational excellence, resource planning, and growth at scale.
Manages and oversees the comprehensive enterprise information security (InfoSec) program to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the company’s platforms, data, applications, networks, systems, servers, and endpoints in an operationally efficient and effective manner.
Leads security operations, monitoring, and incident response in partnership with the company’s managed SOC/EDR provider; performs risk analysis for existing and potential partners and providers.
Owns regulatory and audit compliance, including SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 evidence, the risk register, internal controls matrix, and coordination with external auditors and cyber-insurance carriers.
Directs enterprise IT service delivery, endpoint management, identity and access management, and end-user enablement across a distributed, multi-country workforce.
Leads the technology and security integration of acquired businesses, including identity, email, SSO, security-baseline alignment, backup/DR readiness, and vendor consolidation.
Establishes and enforces a Microsoft-first enterprise tooling strategy and AI governance framework (e.g., Microsoft 365, Purview, Copilot, Azure AI Foundry) with clear governance guardrails for approved AI tools.
Oversees management of third-party vendors in collaboration with Finance — including software, IT hardware, desktop services, telephony, managed services, data center, and network services — and enforces IT procurement and spend-governance policy.
Develops, submits, and manages the operational and capital budget requirements for technology solutions; submits regular progress reports on timeliness, performance, quality, and cost.
Oversees and governs Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery planning for all IT assets and systems.
Institutes and enforces security policy, frameworks, and procedures; balances information assurance with productivity; ensures regulatory compliance; and educates staff on the ethical and secure use of company resources.
Attracts, develops, mentors, and retains top technology and security talent; builds a resilient team structure that minimizes single points of failure.
Supports a culture of client service, continual improvement, and cross-functional collaboration within IT and throughout the company; serves as a role model of integrity and results-oriented focus.

Qualifications

Technology leadership background including experience serving as CIO, VP of IT, or Head of IT, with a proven track record of leading people and managing departmental operations and finances. Expertise implementing InfoSec policies and solutions is of critical importance.
Proven experience leading enterprise IT and security in a regulated, multi-entity, and/or multi-country environment; experience with SaaS, HCM, payroll, or healthcare-adjacent businesses preferred.
Demonstrated experience owning SOC 1 / SOC 2 (or comparable) audit and compliance programs.
Proven experience leading digital enterprise transformation and implementing modern technologies such as cloud, identity, data/analytics, and AI to enable productivity and growth at scale.
Experience leading post-acquisition technology integration (identity, email, SSO, security baseline, vendor consolidation).
Strong project management, vendor management, and budget-management skills.
Excellent business acumen combined with creative problem-solving and analytical skills; a strategic thinker able to see beyond what is and imagine what should be.
Strong negotiator and communicator, able to build credibility with senior business leaders and drive change through influence and persuasion.
High degree of entrepreneurial spirit and initiative; willing to “roll up sleeves” and operate hands-on.
Ability to attract, develop, mentor, and retain top technology talent; sophisticated approach to multi-stakeholder relationship management.
Occasional travel to Viventium facilities (including Costa Rica) and industry conferences.
